name: Conceptual Physics Bank v2 Course Profile
role: Current Framework-declared Physics Bank-v2 contract for Steps 2A, 3A, 3B, and 3C plus downstream Bank-aware builds. Universal procedure remains PM-owned; universal question structures remain owned by _question_structure/. This profile supersedes legacy Bank-profile behavior retained in older Framework summary text.
compatibility_note: Bank-v2 is the current Physics Bank architecture. The legacy bank_course_profile.json is deprecated and must not be used for Bank-v2 mapping, authoring, or canonical Bank reads. Prior stage ZIPs are transport artifacts only, never canonical inputs.

canonical_source_routing.prior_stage_zip_rule: Do not search File Library, uploads, chat attachments, staging folders, or repository history for prior Bank stage ZIPs. unitN.zip is handoff/output only and is discarded as an authority after extraction and sync.
canonical_source_routing.declared_source_rule: Resolve declared curriculum authorities directly through pinned manifests and exact repository paths. Do not use generic web search, repository-wide search, File Library search, or prior ZIP discovery to locate or substitute known authorities.
canonical_source_routing.external_research_rule: Outside research is not part of normal Bank-v2 authoring and is permitted only when the teacher explicitly requests it in the current job.

instructional_spine.hard_rule: Exact Unit Assessment Plan I-can statements are the atomic planning and routing addresses. Build evidence/family plans from I-cans first; never fill destination counts and attach I-can labels afterward.
instructional_spine.execution_rule: question_structure_id, response_mode, representation_mode, evidence_job, and tool route are executable requirements. Metadata agreement without rendered compliance is a FAIL.

record_modes.exact_content: Bank authoring stores one exact canonical prompt/answer/solution. Downstream artifacts reproduce that item exactly unless a later artifact is explicitly allowed to adapt Bank source material.
record_modes.family_seed: Bank authoring stores one complete canonical seed prompt/answer/solution plus an explicit transformation contract. Downstream artifacts may create only validated controlled variants.

wtc.rule: One difficult coherent multipart FRQ-decomposition routine, normally 3-5 connected labeled parts, built around one shared stimulus/representation. May use prior, current, or future Physics content and does not satisfy current-Unit I-can coverage.
wtc.rigor_hard_gate: Every WTC must include an actual evidence-bearing representation or rich shared stimulus, at least one interpretation/extraction move, at least one dependency or use of an earlier conclusion, and at least one planning/model-choice/justification move. It is not a loose preview list.
wtc.untaught_content_rule: When WTC content has not yet been taught, students may be asked to unpack, annotate, interpret, plan, select a relationship, or predict at a structurally accessible level rather than demonstrate mastery of an untaught procedure.

example_yti.rule: Every exact section I-can receives at least one complete Example/YTI pair before any enrichment pair is allocated. Example models; YTI gives a comparable application. When a target supports quantitative/model work, do not crowd it out with generic vocabulary filler.

practice.mix_rule: The 30-family section pool is I-can/evidence-responsive. Decide the family mix only AFTER mapping the exact section I-cans and evidence jobs. No family type has a universal minimum or maximum. A category may be zero when the section does not naturally support it. Do not force quantitative/modeling, vocabulary, representation, or any other category merely to satisfy a mix target.
practice.selection_rule: Each downstream Practice set selects 24 of the 30 families using hard I-can/evidence/representation constraints first, then stable deterministic tie-breaking. Preserve any intentionally mapped section-specific composition, but do not impose a universal category quota. No uncontrolled randomness.
practice.rotation_rule: Different set keys should rotate omissions when constraints allow so the 30-family pool provides real breadth. Rotation preference may never override I-can coverage, family-type constraints, or question quality.
practice.seed_rule: Each family is authored as one complete canonical seed question with answer/solution and transformation metadata. Downstream variants may not be generated from metadata alone.
practice.quantitative_modeling_gate: Use quantitative/modeling families only when the exact I-can/evidence job genuinely calls for mathematical relationship use, calculation, model interpretation, comparison, or quantitative reasoning. Do not manufacture an equation/quantitative task for a vocabulary/conceptual target just to fill a category.

cyu.rule: Keep six exact canonical CYU items per section. They are concise checks, but they must still execute the mapped question structure and representation. Selected-response CYU must visibly render complete answer choices.

warmups.q4_hard_rule: Use a short concrete physical situation that naturally supplies measurements. Supply an appropriate relationship/formula when useful. Students use, rearrange/invert, interpret, or combine the relationship. Do not use naked variable assignments as the normal student experience.
warmups.repetition_rule: Controlled retrieval repetition is allowed and often desirable.

exit.selection_rule: For a declared Exit build key, deterministically select four families that collectively give the strongest feasible section evidence. The selected family IDs define the evidence blueprint for A/B/C; the three forms are controlled secure instances of that same blueprint.
exit.suggested_family_balance: When supported by the section I-cans, include core understanding, conceptual reasoning, quantitative/application, and transfer/representation evidence. This is a best-fit shape, not a rigid universal quota.
exit.security_rule: A/B/C preserve family I-can, evidence job, structure, response demand, and approximate difficulty while requiring genuinely fresh secure stimulus/context/data/representation as appropriate. Exposed instructional finished prompts may not be reused.

A.rule: Map exact family IDs at Step 2A. V1-V4 are controlled parallel secure instances of this same evidence blueprint.

B.rule: Map exact family IDs at Step 2A. V5-V6 are controlled secure instances of a materially alternate/makeup blueprint.

summative.blueprint_overlap_rule: Blueprint A and B may overlap on high-leverage I-cans/families when justified, but Blueprint B must be materially alternate overall in evidence families, contexts, representations, and/or dependency paths. Do not force disjointness if it weakens coverage.
summative.coverage_rule: Every Summative form must be able to directly sample every exact Unit I-can at least once; remaining slots are intentionally weighted toward high-leverage/compound mastery evidence.
summative.security_rule: No exposed instructional finished prompt reuse. Same-family secure variants must preserve tested evidence and approximate difficulty while changing the allowed secure-instance axes.
summative.answer_position_rule: Deterministic selected-response answer-position scrambling remains a downstream final assembly step after content is fixed.

games.rule: Treat these as downstream derivatives/selections from nonsecure Practice family content when the course workflow calls for them; do not inflate the canonical Bank-v2 family inventory merely to store game permutations.

selected_response.hard_rule: A selected-response record must store and visibly render complete choices in student_html. Missing choices, placeholder choices, duplicate choices, or an unkeyed answer are FAIL.

small_data_tables.html_rule: Render real semantic HTML tables. For small value/data tables use the existing Base CSS compact class `values` (`<table class="values">`). Do not use pipe-delimited text and do not stretch a tiny table across the page.

graphs.hard_rule: When the mapped graph is supported by the registered graph tool, use that tool and its styling unchanged. An improvised substitute graph is FAIL.
graphs.qa: Inspect the actual rendered graph for scale, labels, units, plotted relationship/data, readability, and answer-neutrality.

diagrams_vectors_fbd.hard_rule: Do not replace a required diagram/FBD/vector/model with prose. Do not PASS a generic placeholder route. A non-student-constructed diagram must resolve either to an exact canonical asset at a pinned path or to a registered deterministic diagram tool. If neither exists, redesign that slot to an evidence-equivalent non-diagram task only when the I-can permits it; otherwise fail closed and report the missing route.

route_contract.canonical_asset: Record an exact repository, pinned commit, canonical asset path, and asset_id when available. A generic phrase such as framework_approved_diagram_route is NOT an executable route.
route_contract.registered_tool: Record a tool_key that resolves through Tools/MANIFEST.json plus the parameter/answer-neutrality contract needed to generate the representation. If the tool is not registered, it is not a canonical production route.
route_contract.student_constructed: A student-constructed diagram may use an explicit blank HTML/CSS response surface without a completed diagram generator, provided the prompt itself supplies a sufficient physical situation and no answer is leaked.

rendering_and_tool_contract.representation_presence: If representation_mode requires a graph/table/diagram/vector/model/image, student_html must contain the usable representation. Metadata-only compliance is FAIL.

evidence_response_representation_alignme.hard_rule: The evidence_job states what the student must actually do. response_mode and representation_mode must allow the student to produce or select evidence of that action. A map record fails when its metadata describes one student action but its response/representation can only collect a different action.
evidence_response_representation_alignme.construction_rule: If the I-can/evidence_job says draw, construct, build, create, or produce a representation, the default route is constructed_response with an explicit student response surface and the corresponding student_constructed representation mode. selected_response is allowed only when the evidence job is intentionally rewritten as identify/select/critique/compare a supplied representation rather than construct one.
evidence_response_representation_alignme.selected_response_rule: A selected-response item may ask students to identify, choose, classify, compare, interpret, or critique. Do not label a selected-response item as evidence that the student constructed/drew/built something.

practice_family_contract.anti_drift_rule: A variant fails if it changes the I-can, evidence job, structure, intended reasoning, approximate difficulty, or required representation behavior. A noun/name swap alone is not meaningful variation when the family requires richer change.

deterministic_selection.hard_rule: Constrained first, deterministic tie-break second. Never ask the model to choose randomly.
deterministic_selection.reproducibility: Same pinned Bank identity and same build key must yield the same family IDs and same ordering before any final answer-choice scramble.
deterministic_selection.tie_break: Stable hash/pseudo-random ordering of eligible family IDs after hard constraints are satisfied.
hard_constraints_precede_tie_break: mapped section-specific family composition only when intentionally required by the evidence architecture

physics_authoring_rules.short_by_default: Extra context only when it improves the Physics, evidence, or authenticity of the situation.
physics_authoring_rules.physical_math: Do not author naked plug-and-chug prompts that only assign variables. Begin with a concrete physical situation/phenomenon that naturally supplies measurements; equations are relationships describing that phenomenon.
physics_authoring_rules.conceptual_before_computational: Establish the physical model/relationship qualitatively before formula substitution when the concept supports it.
physics_authoring_rules.representations: Graphs, diagrams, FBDs, vectors, motion diagrams, tables, models, and other representations are evidence when they carry the task, not decoration.
physics_authoring_rules.multi_step: Multi-step means an intermediate result is actually required for the final result.
physics_authoring_rules.source_neutrality: Use only current manifest-/Framework-declared curriculum sources for normal Bank authoring. Do not search File Library, uploads, prior stage ZIPs, old copies, or generic web sources to locate or supplement known Bank authorities. Outside research requires an explicit teacher request in the current job.

hard_failures: family/content mode forced only to satisfy a category quota rather than fit the I-can/evidence job
evidence_job cannot actually be demonstrated through the mapped response_mode/representation_mode
construct/draw/build evidence mapped as selected_response without changing the evidence job to selection/critique
generic diagram/FBD/vector placeholder route without an exact canonical asset or registered deterministic tool
mapped question structure not executed by the final prompt
pipe-delimited/plain-text pseudo-table used as final data table
supported graph improvised instead of using registered graph_tool
graph/diagram/table visually unreadable or physically incorrect
WTC is a loose set of independent preview questions rather than a coherent connected FRQ routine
qa.regeneration_rule: If a generated downstream variant fails family fidelity, regenerate/repair that item within the declared family contract; do not silently substitute a different family or weaken the evidence job.
